scope: For every fixed compact connected Hermitian background with zero lower Monge--Ampere mass, an explicit positive-radius ball of smooth probability log-densities around log(h^n/(V_h*dV)) in C^(2,alpha), 0<alpha<1, has unique exact Gauduchon maximizing currents with uniformly bounded probability and determinant densities in Linfinity and therefore at n/(n-1). The family is infinite dimensional, contains distinct data with distinct exact maximizers, and imposes no bounds on higher derivatives. Broader continuous or large bounded families remain open.

exact_task.problem:
Let X be a connected compact complex manifold of dimension n>=3, h a smooth positive Hermitian form, and dV a smooth positive probability volume. Suppose the bounded-potential lower Monge-Ampere mass v_-(h) is zero. Use dd^c=(i/(2 pi))partial barpartial. Let G_h be the positive (n-1,n-1)-currents T with dd^c T=0 and integral h wedge T=1. In an h-unitary frame, write sigma_T=h wedge T and the positive Hermitian matrix density P_T characterized by beta wedge T=(1/n)tr(B P_T)d sigma_T, tr P_T=n, where B is the matrix of a smooth (1,1)-form beta relative to h. For a real continuous logarithmic density F, set Gamma_F(T)=(exp(F)dV/h^n)^(1/n) det(P_T)^(1/n) sigma_T and D_F(T)=Gamma_F(T)(X). The attained maximum M(F)>0 equals exp(-B_0(F)/n), where B_0(F) is the scalar in MA_h(u)=exp(B_0(F)+F)dV. For every exact maximizing current T, the determinant-weighted probability nu_(T,F)=Gamma_F(T)/M(F) is absolutely continuous with respect to dV and represents an adjoint/supporting probability of B_0. If F is smooth, the exact maximizing current is unique, smooth and strictly positive: it is the normalized (n-1)st power of the Gauduchon form conformal to the smooth solution form. In the smooth case Gamma_F(T)=exp(F/n)k_T dV with k_T=(gamma^n/dV)^((n-1)/n) for T=gamma^(n-1), respecting trace normalization. At an actual maximizer one can equivalently define its determinant density by k_T=exp(-F/n)M(F)d nu_(T,F)/dV.

Original S17 asks whether a uniform critical L^(n/(n-1)) estimate can hold for the determinant-weighted probabilities of exact maximizing currents representing adjoints, uniformly as F ranges over a specified bounded set, when v_-(h)=0. Identify geometric or density hypotheses giving such a restricted estimate. Specify the bounded family, its topology/quantitative bounds, whether all its data are smooth or continuous, and whether the estimated density is k_T or d nu_(T,F)/dV. The endpoint can fail for the full normalized Gauduchon test family, whereas every strictly smaller exponent has a universal estimate. Positive lower mass gives the full endpoint, but is excluded here. One fixed smooth strictly positive density has a unique smooth maximizer; this fact is background and is not a uniform theorem over a family. Near-maximizing sequences can have divergent higher moments even on Kahler manifolds. Distinguish exact maximizers from all tests and from near-maximizers. No candidate density family, geometric condition, estimate or proof is supplied.

A single datum, finite list, mere constant shifts, the known full-family failure, or a statement about near-maximizers does not solve the uniform exact-maximizer problem. Two contractions give an explicit radius in terms of linear elliptic inverse norms; no lower-MA-mass assumption is used.
notes.detailedSummary: Fix 0<alpha<1, H=h^n/dV, V=integral h^n, and F*=log(H/V). Linear elliptic Fredholm theory and the maximum principle give a positive smooth chi_0 with dd^c(chi_0 h^{n-1})=0 and integral chi_0 h^n=1. The maps (v,c)->L_h v-c, with integral v dV=0 and L_h v=n dd^c v wedge h^{n-1}/h^n, and eta->dd^c(eta h^{n-1})/dV, with integral eta h^n=0, have bounded inverses K and G in the indicated Hölder spaces. Constants D,Q,C_A control dd^c, the quadratic log-determinant remainder, and the perturbation of the Gauduchon operator. Set m=min chi_0, C_0=||chi_0||_{C^{2,alpha}}, r=min{1/(2D),1/(4KQ),m/(4G C_A D C_0)}, and epsilon=r/(2K). For every smooth F with ||F-F*||_{C^{2,alpha}}<=epsilon, contraction yields a smooth u, integral u dV=0, and c, with ||u||_{C^{4,alpha}}+|c|<=r, solving (h+dd^c u)^n=exp(F+log V+c)dV. The form omega=h+dd^c u satisfies h/2<=omega<=3h/2. A second, linear contraction produces the unique normalized solution chi of dd^c(chi omega^{n-1})=0, integral chi h^n=1, with ||chi-chi_0||_{C^{2,alpha}}<=m/2. In particular m/2<=chi and chi<=3 max(chi_0)/2. All constants are finite for every smooth positive h, including any h with v_-(h)=0. No global Hermitian Monge-Ampere estimate or positive lower mass theorem is invoked.
notes.text:
QUANTITATIVE LOCAL SOLUTION AND GAUDUCHON CONSTRUCTION

Fix the connected compact complex manifold and smooth positive h,dV in the question. Fix 0<alpha<1. All functions and forms below are real where appropriate. Set
  H=h^n/dV,   V=integral_X h^n,   F*=log(H/V),   b*=log V.
Thus exp(F*)dV=h^n/V is a probability measure. The convention is exactly dd^c=(i/(2 pi))partial barpartial.

We prove the following local assertion, without using v_-(h). There is a quantitatively specified epsilon>0 such that every smooth F satisfying ||F-F*||_{C^{2,alpha}}<=epsilon has a smooth solution
  omega=h+dd^c u,   omega^n=exp(F+b)dV,
with integral u dV=0, b=b*+c, and uniform bounds on u,c. Moreover omega has a uniformly controlled positive factor chi with dd^c(chi omega^{n-1})=0. The constants and proof follow.

1. Linear elliptic facts and the baseline factor.

Use fixed Hölder norms from a finite smooth atlas and background connections. We use the foundational facts for real smooth scalar uniformly elliptic second-order operators on a compact manifold without boundary: the Schauder estimate
  ||v||_{C^{s+2,alpha}} <= C (||Pv||_{C^{s,alpha}}+||v||_{C^0}),
distributional elliptic regularity, and the strong maximum principle. The relevant hypotheses are checked below. Here is also the Fredholm argument needed, rather than an extra complex-geometric existence theorem. The Schauder estimate, compact embedding into C^0, and local elliptic regularity give finite-dimensional kernel, closed range, and finite-dimensional cokernel represented by smooth solutions of the formal adjoint. A scalar operator with positive-definite principal symbol has index zero: deform its principal coefficients through positive-definite symbols to those of a real Laplacian and its lower-order coefficients to those of that Laplacian. The operators remain elliptic Fredholm throughout, their index is constant, and the Laplacian has index zero. The usual local Schauder input itself is obtained by the constant-coefficient Hölder estimate, freezing principal coefficients on sufficiently small coordinate balls, absorbing the coefficient error, and using a partition of unity. These are foundational real elliptic facts; no global complex Monge-Ampere regularity or mass result is needed here.

Define
  L_h v = n (dd^c v wedge h^{n-1})/h^n.
Its principal symbol is positive definite since h is positive, its coefficients are smooth, and it has no zeroth-order term. Connectedness and the strong maximum principle imply that its kernel consists precisely of constants. Its index is zero, so its cokernel is one dimensional. Let p be a nonzero real smooth generator of the kernel of its formal adjoint relative to dV.

The function p has one sign. Indeed, the range of L_h contains no nonzero nonnegative smooth function: L_h v>=0 on a compact manifold implies v is constant by the strong maximum principle. If p took both signs, one could choose nonnegative smooth functions supported where p is positive and negative, and a nonzero nonnegative linear combination g with integral g p dV=0. The one-dimensional Fredholm compatibility condition would give g=L_h v, a contradiction. Choose the sign so p>=0. It is actually strictly positive. In any real coordinate patch the adjoint has the form a^{ij}partial_ij+b^i partial_i+c_0 with positive-definite a. Subtract a constant C>=max{0,sup c_0} from its zeroth-order coefficient. The resulting operator P has nonpositive zeroth-order coefficient and Pp=-Cp<=0. If p vanished at an interior point, the strong minimum principle would make p identically zero; connectedness contradicts its choice. Normalize integral p dV=1.

Define chi_0=p/H. Integration by parts gives
  integral L_h v p dV = n integral v dd^c(chi_0 h^{n-1}),
so
  dd^c(chi_0 h^{n-1})=0,   integral chi_0 h^n=1.
In particular chi_0 is smooth and strictly positive. This reconstructs the baseline Gauduchon factor, rather than requiring a specialized external Gauduchon existence citation. The probability mu_0=chi_0 h^n is the compatibility measure for L_h.

Let E_4={v in C^{4,alpha}: integral v dV=0}. The map
  A:E_4 x R -> C^{2,alpha},   A(v,c)=L_h v-c,
is an isomorphism. For a prescribed g, necessarily c=-integral g dmu_0; then L_h v=g-integral g dmu_0 is solvable by the Fredholm compatibility condition, and its constant is uniquely fixed by the dV-mean-zero normalization. Schauder estimates and the bounded inverse theorem give a finite inverse norm K. Take K>=1 and the product norm ||v||_{C^{4,alpha}}+|c|.

For a positive smooth (1,1)-form omega define
  A_omega eta = dd^c(eta omega^{n-1})/dV.
At omega=h its formal adjoint relative to dV is
  eta -> (dd^c eta wedge h^{n-1})/dV = (H/n)L_h eta.
This has kernel constants and index zero. Therefore A_h has one-dimensional kernel, spanned by chi_0, and range
  Z_0={g in C^{0,alpha}: integral g dV=0}.
Its restriction to
  E_chi={eta in C^{2,alpha}: integral eta h^n=0}
is an isomorphism onto Z_0. Let R be its inverse and G>=1 a bound for its operator norm. All the operators here have smooth coefficients and uniformly elliptic principal symbols, so all the elliptic hypotheses just used hold.

2. Quantitative nonlinear constants.

Choose the form and endomorphism Hölder norms so endomorphism composition is submultiplicative and their norms dominate pointwise operator norms. Scaling the usual norms by their multiplication constants achieves this. Let D>=1 satisfy, for every v,
  ||dd^c v||_{C^{2,alpha}} <= D ||v||_{C^{4,alpha}},
  ||h^{-1}dd^c v||_{C^{2,alpha},alg} <= D ||v||_{C^{4,alpha}}.
Let C_tr>=1 bound the trace map in these norms and set Q=2 C_tr D^2. For ||v||_{C^{4,alpha}}<=1/(2D), define
  N(v)=log det(I+h^{-1}dd^c v)-L_h v.
The convergent Banach-algebra power series
  N(v)=sum_{j>=2} (-1)^{j+1} tr((h^{-1}dd^c v)^j)/j
shows
  ||N(v)||_{C^{2,alpha}} <= Q ||v||_{C^{4,alpha}}^2,
and, for v,w in this ball,
  ||N(v)-N(w)||_{C^{2,alpha}}
    <= Q (||v||_{C^{4,alpha}}+||w||_{C^{4,alpha}})
           ||v-w||_{C^{4,alpha}}.
For example, the difference estimate follows by telescoping each matrix power and summing sum_{j>=2}rho^{j-1}=rho/(1-rho), with rho<=1/2. These constants depend only on the fixed norms and h.

Choose C_A>=1 so that whenever ||omega-h||_{C^{2,alpha}}<=1,
  ||A_omega-A_h||_{C^{2,alpha}->C^{0,alpha}}
       <= C_A ||omega-h||_{C^{2,alpha}}.
This is a direct polynomial estimate, not an unproved regularity assumption: expand omega^{n-1}-h^{n-1}, multiply by eta, and apply dd^c. The Hölder product estimates use at most two derivatives of omega. A finite C_A is determined by n,h,dV and the fixed norms.

Set
  m=min_X chi_0>0,   C_0=||chi_0||_{C^{2,alpha}},
  r=min{1/(2D), 1/(4KQ), m/(4G C_A D C_0)},
  epsilon=r/(2K).
The norms dominate supremum norms, so m<=C_0. These formulas specify positive constants solely from the fixed background. In particular they contain no v_-(h) term or inverse lower-mass bound.

3. First contraction: the solution form.

Put f=F-F*. On the closed radius-r ball in E_4 x R consider
  Psi_f(v,c)=A^{-1}(f-N(v)).
The norm estimates above show
  ||Psi_f(v,c)|| <= K epsilon+KQ r^2 <= 3r/4,
and its Lipschitz constant is at most 2KQr<=1/2. The contraction theorem yields (u,c) with
  ||u||_{C^{4,alpha}}+|c|<=r,
  log(omega^n/h^n)-c=f,   omega=h+dd^c u.
Consequently omega^n=exp(F+b*+c)dV. Since the pointwise operator norm of h^{-1}dd^c u is at most Dr<=1/2,
  (1/2)h <= omega <= (3/2)h.
For smooth F this solution is smooth. To verify the bootstrap, differentiate the local log-determinant equation: its linearization has principal coefficients omega^{-1}, uniformly positive, and the initial coefficients are C^{2,alpha}. Schauder estimates on differentiated equations improve regularity of u; iteration with smooth F,h gives all derivatives. This uses only the same local linear elliptic theory. No estimates uniform in higher derivatives of F are asserted or needed.

4. Second contraction: the Gauduchon factor.

Let delta=||A_omega-A_h||<=C_A D r. Since each A_omega has integral zero, the right side below lies in Z_0. Write chi=chi_0+eta with eta in E_chi and solve
  eta=-R(A_omega-A_h)(chi_0+eta).
The affine map is a contraction on E_chi, since
  G delta <= m/(4C_0)<=1/4.
It therefore has exactly one solution, and
  ||eta||_{C^{2,alpha}}
    <= G delta C_0/(1-G delta)
    <=2G C_A D r C_0 <=m/2.
Hence
  dd^c(chi omega^{n-1})=0,   integral chi h^n=1,
  chi>=m/2,   chi<=chi_0+m/2 <=(3/2)max_X chi_0.
The factor is smooth by linear elliptic bootstrapping because omega is smooth. Moreover it is the unique C^{2,alpha} solution with integral chi h^n=1: the same global affine contraction equation holds for any such solution.

This finishes the local construction. Every prerequisite has been obtained from smooth positivity, compactness, connectedness, and foundational linear elliptic theory. In particular the construction is equally valid on the given h when v_-(h)=0.

correctness.report:
The argument is valid conditional on the standard elliptic premises listed below. The principal symbols of L_h, A_h and their adjoints are positive definite; compactness makes ellipticity uniform. The maximum principle gives ker L_h = constants, and index zero gives the stated one-dimensional compatibility space. The sign argument for p is sound. Strict positivity follows by applying the maximum principle to -p after replacing the adjoint's zeroth-order coefficient c_0 by c_0-C.

Both inverse maps have the claimed domains, normalizations and ranges. The logarithmic remainder estimates follow from the Banach-algebra series and telescoping powers. The chosen radius ensures Dr<=1/2, KQr<=1/4 and G C_A Dr<=m/(4C_0), which respectively give positivity, the first contraction and the positive normalized Gauduchon factor. Smoothness for smooth F follows by differentiating the uniformly elliptic equation and applying local Schauder estimates; no uniform higher-derivative estimate is asserted.

No lower-mass theorem is used, so applicability to the assumed zero-mass background is conditional only on that background existing, not on a positive lower-mass bound. The detailed summary matches the full statement. The correction merely makes explicit that the short summary's neighborhood means its smooth-data slice; it does not assert smoothing for arbitrary C^{2,alpha} data. The full proof is unchanged. The notes do not supply primary-source citations for the foundational elliptic inputs; those inputs are isolated as exact premises for source validation.
premises: Let M be a compact smooth manifold without boundary, dμ a smooth positive density, 0<α<1, and s a nonnegative integer. Let P be a real scalar second-order differential operator with smooth coefficients and uniformly positive-definite symmetric principal coefficient matrix. Then P:C^{s+2,α}(M)→C^{s,α}(M) is Fredholm, its kernel consists of smooth functions, and its range is exactly the set of f satisfying ∫_M f p dμ=0 for every smooth p with P* p=0, where P* is the formal adjoint relative to dμ. Moreover, ||v||_{C^{s+2,α}}≤C(||Pv||_{C^{s,α}}+||v||_{C^0}) for a constant determined by P, M and the fixed norms. The analogous interior Schauder estimates hold on coordinate domains for uniformly elliptic operators whose coefficients belong to C^{s,α}.
Let M be a smooth manifold and P a scalar differential operator of order two with smooth coefficients and elliptic principal symbol. If a distribution v satisfies Pv∈C^∞ locally, then v∈C^∞ locally.

The Fredholm index is constant along a continuous path of Fredholm operators between fixed Banach spaces. On a compact smooth manifold without boundary, the Laplace–Beltrami operator of any smooth Riemannian metric, acting from C^{s+2,α} to C^{s,α} for a nonnegative integer s and 0<α<1, is Fredholm of index zero.

Let Ω be a connected domain in a smooth real manifold and P=a^{ij}∂_i∂_j+b^i∂_i+c a scalar second-order operator with smooth coefficients, positive-definite principal matrix locally uniformly on Ω, and c≤0. If v∈C^2(Ω), Pv≥0, and v attains a nonnegative maximum at an interior point, then v is constant on Ω. Equivalently, if Pv≤0 and v attains a nonpositive interior minimum, then v is constant.

source.report:
All four exact premise strings are established. For premise 0, I reconstructed the stated Hölder-space version from Oh’s compact-manifold Sobolev Fredholm theorem, Dyatlov’s smooth-kernel result, and Simon’s interior Schauder estimates. Closed-range duality and distributional elliptic regularity identify the cokernel with smooth solutions of the formal adjoint relative to dμ. Differentiation, interpolation, and a finite coordinate cover give the stated higher-order Schauder estimates, including the C^{s,α}-coefficient interior variant. [Oh, Proposition 10.1.13](https://cgp.ibs.re.kr/~yongoh/all.pdf), [Simon, Lecture 12](https://math.stanford.edu/~lms/lecs-on-pde.pdf).

Premise 1 follows from Cass’s Theorem 7.1, localized in manifold charts. Premise 2 follows from local constancy of the Banach-space Fredholm index; the Laplace–Beltrami index is zero because its kernel and adjoint kernel coincide, with the Hölder realization preserving these smooth kernels. [Cass](https://www.math.ubc.ca/~cass/research/pdf/FS.pdf), [Analysis on Manifolds, Theorem 1.5.2](https://www.staff.science.uu.nl/~ban00101/geoman2017/AS-2017.pdf).

Premise 3 matches the c≤0 strong maximum principle, with the minimum formulation obtained by replacing v with −v. Its applications to L_h and the shifted adjoint have the required ellipticity and signs. [MIT, Lecture 6, Theorem 4](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-156-differential-analysis-spring-2004/d9e0f047d5682a70799331a926d27a11_lec6.pdf). No positive lower Monge–Ampère mass hypothesis is required by these external results.

Writing E_χ={η∈C^{2,α}(X,ℝ):∫_X ηh^n=0}, the restriction A_h:E_χ→Z_0 is an isomorphism. Let R:Z_0→E_χ be its inverse and choose G≥1 with ‖R‖≤G.

Choose the form and endomorphism Hölder norms to dominate pointwise norms, and the endomorphism norm ‖·‖_{C^{2,α},alg} to be submultiplicative. Choose D≥1 and C_tr≥1 such that, for every v∈C^{4,α},
‖dd^cv‖_{C^{2,α}}≤D‖v‖_{C^{4,α}},
‖h^{-1}dd^cv‖_{C^{2,α},alg}≤D‖v‖_{C^{4,α}},
and ‖tr U‖_{C^{2,α}}≤C_tr‖U‖_{C^{2,α},alg}.
Set Q=2C_trD^2. For ‖v‖_{C^{4,α}}≤1/(2D), define
N(v)=log det(I+h^{-1}dd^cv)−L_hv.
Then
‖N(v)‖_{C^{2,α}}≤Q‖v‖_{C^{4,α}}^2,
and, for all v,w in this ball,
‖N(v)−N(w)‖_{C^{2,α}}≤Q(‖v‖_{C^{4,α}}+‖w‖_{C^{4,α}})‖v−w‖_{C^{4,α}}.
There exists a finite C_A≥1, determined by the fixed background and norms, such that every smooth positive ω with ‖ω−h‖_{C^{2,α}}≤1 satisfies
‖A_ω−A_h‖_{C^{2,α}→C^{0,α}}≤C_A‖ω−h‖_{C^{2,α}}.

Put
m=min_Xχ_0>0,  C_0=‖χ_0‖_{C^{2,α}},
r=min{1/(2D), 1/(4KQ), m/(4GC_ADC_0)},
ε=r/(2K)>0.
All these constants are determined by X,h,dV,α and the fixed norms, with no lower Monge–Ampère mass bound entering their definitions.

For every smooth real F with ‖F−F_*‖_{C^{2,α}}≤ε, without any requirement that ∫_X e^F dV=1, there exist u∈C^∞(X,ℝ) and c∈ℝ such that
∫_X u dV=0,  ‖u‖_{C^{4,α}}+|c|≤r,
ω=h+dd^cu,  b=b_*+c,
ω^n=e^{F+b}dV,
(1/2)h≤ω≤(3/2)h,  ‖ω−h‖_{C^{2,α}}≤Dr.
For this ω there is a unique χ∈C^{2,α}(X,ℝ) satisfying
A_ωχ=0,  ∫_X χh^n=1.
It is smooth and strictly positive. If δ=‖A_ω−A_h‖_{C^{2,α}→C^{0,α}}, then
δ≤C_ADr,  Gδ≤m/(4C_0)≤1/4,
‖χ−χ_0‖_{C^{2,α}}≤GδC_0/(1−Gδ)≤2GC_ADrC_0≤m/2.
In particular,
dd^c(χω^{n-1})=0,
m/2≤χ(x)≤χ_0(x)+m/2≤(3/2)max_Xχ_0  for all x∈X.
No uniform estimates on higher derivatives of F,u, or χ are assumed or asserted.
reconstruction.proof:
All the elliptic operators below are real scalar operators on the underlying compact real manifold of X. Their principal symbols are positive definite: contraction of dd^c of a real function with a positive Hermitian form is a positive constant multiple of a positive-definite real second-order symbol. Thus the stated elliptic premises apply with the indicated Hölder spaces. We use Stokes' identity in the form ∫ f dd^c S=∫ dd^c f∧S for smooth complementary-degree forms; the identity also holds when f is C^2.

1. The reference adjoint factor and the two linear inverses.

In an h-unitary frame, L_hv=tr(h^{-1}dd^cv). Consequently L_h has smooth coefficients, positive-definite principal symbol, and no zeroth-order term. Its kernel on C^{s+2,α}, for any nonnegative integer s, consists of constants. Indeed, a kernel element is smooth by the permitted elliptic regularity, and subtracting its maximum gives a function with an interior maximum zero; the permitted strong maximum principle, with c=0, makes it constant. Connectedness is used here.

Choose a smooth Riemannian metric and its Laplacian with positive principal coefficient matrix. The convex path between this Laplacian and L_h has positive-definite principal matrices and smooth coefficients throughout. Each member is Fredholm on C^{s+2,α}→C^{s,α} by the stated Fredholm premise. The path is continuous between these fixed Banach spaces, so index invariance and the index-zero Laplacian premise give index(L_h)=0. Since the kernel has dimension one, the cokernel has dimension one. The supplied range characterization therefore implies that the smooth kernel of the formal adjoint relative to dV is one-dimensional. Choose a nonzero real generator p.

We prove its positivity rather than assuming an adjoint maximum principle with an uncontrolled zeroth-order term. First p cannot take both positive and negative values. Otherwise choose nonnegative smooth bumps in its positive and negative regions. By adding sufficiently large multiples of these bumps to the constant function 1, one obtains strictly positive smooth functions g_+ and g_- for which ∫g_+p dV>0 and ∫g_-p dV<0. A convex combination is a strictly positive smooth g satisfying ∫gp dV=0. The Fredholm range characterization would give L_hv=g. At a maximum of v, however, L_hv≤0, a contradiction. Replacing p by -p if necessary, we thus have p≥0 and p not identically zero.

Write the smooth formal adjoint locally as L_h^*=a^{ij}∂_i∂_j+\widetilde b^i∂_i+c. Its principal coefficient matrix is positive definite. Here c=L_h^*1 is a globally defined smooth function. Choose C≥0 with c+C≥0 everywhere and set Q=L_h^*-(c+C). Then Q has zeroth-order coefficient -C≤0 and Qp=-(c+C)p≤0. If p vanished anywhere, it would attain the nonpositive minimum zero at an interior point. The permitted strong minimum principle would make p identically zero on the connected manifold, a contradiction. Hence p>0. Normalize it by ∫p dV=1; this determines it uniquely.

Set H=h^n/dV, χ_0=p/H, and μ_0=p dV. They are smooth, and χ_0>0. For every smooth real v,
∫L_hv p dV=n∫dd^cv∧χ_0h^{n-1}=n∫v dd^c(χ_0h^{n-1})=0.
Thus dd^c(χ_0h^{n-1})=0, while ∫χ_0h^n=∫p dV=1. This also proves μ_0=χ_0h^n.

Now take s=2. Given g∈C^{2,α}, the equation L_hv-c=g necessarily has
c=-∫g dμ_0,
L_hv=g-∫g dμ_0.
The latter right-hand side is orthogonal to p, so the supplied range theorem gives a solution in C^{4,α}. Subtract its dV mean to place it in E_4. The constant-kernel conclusion proves uniqueness. Thus A:E_4×R→C^{2,α} is bijective.

Its inverse has a finite norm. For completeness, this follows directly from the supplied Schauder estimate. On the mean-zero subspace, the estimate ||v||_{C^{4,α}}≤C(||L_hv||_{C^{2,α}}+||v||_{C^0}) can have its C^0 term removed: otherwise normalize a contradicting sequence by its C^0 norm. The Schauder estimate gives a bounded sequence in C^{4,α}; finite-atlas Arzelà–Ascoli gives a convergent subsequence in lower differentiability. Its limit is a mean-zero kernel element with C^0 norm one, contradicting the constant-kernel conclusion. Since |c|≤||g||_{C^0}, this gives a K≥1 with the asserted product-norm bound.

For any smooth positive ω, the operator A_ωη=dd^c(ηω^{n-1})/dV is scalar second-order, with smooth coefficients and positive-definite principal symbol. Stokes gives ∫A_ωη dV=0. Integration by parts at h gives
A_h^*η=(dd^cη∧h^{n-1})/dV=(H/n)L_hη.
Its smooth kernel therefore consists of constants. The range characterization, now with s=0, gives range(A_h)=Z_0. The same convex-symbol homotopy used above proves index(A_h)=0, so its kernel has dimension one. It contains χ_0, and hence equals Rχ_0. Because ∫χ_0h^n=1, E_χ is a complement to that kernel, and A_h:E_χ→Z_0 is bijective. The s=0 Schauder estimate and the same compactness argument, now on E_χ, give a bounded inverse R. Choose G≥1 bounding its norm. These applications use compactness without boundary and the smooth, uniformly elliptic coefficients established above.

2. Quantitative nonlinear estimates.

Multiplication of C^{2,α} endomorphisms is continuous. Rescaling a usual Hölder norm therefore makes it submultiplicative and makes it dominate the pointwise operator norm. The indicated form norms may likewise be chosen to dominate pointwise norms. The smooth-coefficient maps dd^c and h^{-1}dd^c from C^{4,α} to the stated C^{2,α} spaces are bounded, and trace is bounded. This supplies D,C_tr≥1 as in the statement.

Put U_v=h^{-1}dd^cv. If ||v||_{C^{4,α}}≤1/(2D), then ||U_v||_{C^{2,α},alg}≤1/2. The convergent algebra series for log(I+U_v) gives
N(v)=Σ_{j≥2}((-1)^{j+1}/j)tr(U_v^j).
Pointwise this is the real logarithmic determinant, because U_v is h-self-adjoint and I+U_v is positive. Submultiplicativity gives
||N(v)||_{C^{2,α}}≤C_tr Σ_{j≥2}||U_v||^j/j≤2C_trD^2||v||_{C^{4,α}}^2.
For U=U_v and V=U_w, the telescoping identity for U^j-V^j gives
||U^j-V^j||≤jρ^{j-1}||U-V||,
where ρ=max(||U||,||V||)≤1/2. Summing yields
||N(v)-N(w)||_{C^{2,α}}≤C_tr[ρ/(1-ρ)]||U-V||
≤2C_trD^2(||v||_{C^{4,α}}+||w||_{C^{4,α}})||v-w||_{C^{4,α}}.
These are precisely the asserted bounds with Q=2C_trD^2.

The coefficients of A_ω are obtained by applying at most two derivatives to ω^{n-1}, together with the fixed smooth division by dV. Expanding the difference of the two powers and using Hölder product estimates therefore gives
||A_ω-A_h||_{C^{2,α}→C^{0,α}}≤C_A||ω-h||_{C^{2,α}}
whenever ||ω-h||_{C^{2,α}}≤1. A finite C_A≥1 depends only on the fixed background and norms. This estimate does not require any higher derivatives of ω.

3. Construction of the local Monge–Ampère solution.

All constants defining r and ε are finite and positive; in particular m=minχ_0>0. Let f=F-F_* and write b=log V+c. Since F_*=log(H/V), the desired equation is equivalent to
log det(I+h^{-1}dd^cu)-c=f,
or A(u,c)=f-N(u).
On the closed product-norm ball of radius r in E_4×R define
Φ(u,c)=A^{-1}(f-N(u)).
The radius restrictions and ||f||_{C^{2,α}}≤ε=r/(2K) give
||Φ(u,c)||≤Kε+KQr^2≤r/2+r/4=3r/4.
For two points in this ball,
||Φ(u,c)-Φ(v,d)||≤2KQr||(u,c)-(v,d)||≤(1/2)||(u,c)-(v,d)||.
Iteration from zero remains in the ball and its successive differences form a geometrically summable sequence. Completeness gives a fixed point; the same Lipschitz bound proves uniqueness within the ball. Thus ∫u dV=0 and ||u||_{C^{4,α}}+|c|≤r. Since Dr≤1/2, the pointwise eigenvalues of h^{-1}dd^cu lie in [-1/2,1/2]. Consequently
(1/2)h≤ω=h+dd^cu≤(3/2)h,
||ω-h||_{C^{2,α}}≤Dr,
and ω^n=e^{F+log V+c}dV.

Here u is initially C^{4,α}. We justify its smoothness using only the permitted interior Schauder estimates. In holomorphic coordinates write the equation as log det W(x)=J(x), where W is the positive matrix of h+dd^cu and J is smooth when F is smooth. Suppose u is C^{k,α}, k≥4. For a real coordinate direction and a sufficiently small displacement a, let u_a(x)=[u(x+ae)-u(x)]/a. Subtract the two logarithmic determinant equations. The matrix identity
log det W_1-log det W_0=∫_0^1 tr(((1-θ)W_0+θW_1)^{-1}(W_1-W_0))dθ
shows that u_a solves a linear uniformly elliptic equation. Its coefficients are averages of the inverses of the convex combinations of W(x) and W(x+ae). On fixed smaller coordinate domains these coefficients have uniformly bounded C^{k-2,α} norms and uniformly positive principal matrices, independently of a. Its right-hand side is the difference quotient of smooth J minus the contraction of the difference quotient of the smooth background h with these coefficients; it has uniformly bounded C^{k-2,α} norm. Also ||u_a||_{C^0} is uniformly bounded by ||du||_{C^0}. Each u_a already belongs to C^{k,α}, so the permitted interior Schauder estimate, with s=k-2, supplies a uniform C^{k,α} bound on still smaller domains. Letting a tend to zero, Arzelà–Ascoli and preservation of the Hölder bound show that ∂_e u∈C^{k,α}. Hence u∈C^{k+1,α} locally. Iteration and a finite atlas prove u∈C^∞. This argument neither assumes nor produces a family-uniform estimate involving higher derivatives of F.

4. Construction and estimates for the perturbed adjoint factor.

The resulting ω is smooth, so the operator estimate above applies. Put B=A_ω-A_h and δ=||B||_{C^{2,α}→C^{0,α}}. Stokes implies that B maps C^{2,α} into Z_0. We have
δ≤C_ADr,
Gδ≤m/(4C_0)≤1/4,
since C_0=||χ_0||_{C^{2,α}}≥m. Write χ=χ_0+η with η∈E_χ. The conditions A_ωχ=0 and ∫χh^n=1 are equivalent to
η=-RB(χ_0+η).
On E_χ the norm of RB is at most Gδ<1. The convergent geometric operator series for (I+RB)^{-1} yields a unique η and gives
||χ-χ_0||_{C^{2,α}}≤GδC_0/(1-Gδ)
≤2GC_ADrC_0≤m/2.
This also proves uniqueness among all normalized C^{2,α} solutions, not merely among positive ones. In particular χ≥χ_0-m/2≥m/2>0, and
χ≤χ_0+m/2≤(3/2)max_Xχ_0.
Finally A_ω has smooth coefficients and elliptic principal symbol, and A_ωχ=0 distributionally. The explicitly permitted distributional elliptic regularity gives χ∈C^∞. Its equation is exactly dd^c(χω^{n-1})=0.

This proves every assertion, including the stated estimates and normalizations. No lower Monge–Ampère mass estimate, Gauduchon existence theorem, or other geometric hypothesis was used. Accordingly the argument remains valid under the additional antecedent v_-(h)=0, without purporting to establish that antecedent.

notes.summary: Complete restricted endpoint theorem at zero lower mass: all smooth probability log-densities in the explicit small C^{2,alpha} ball from n1 have uniformly L-infinity bounded exact-maximizer densities, both k_T and dnu/dV. AM-GM plus Stokes proves exact maximality and uniqueness. The normalized family is infinite-dimensional and contains an explicit path of distinct data and distinct exact maximizers on the same zero-mass h. No conclusion for arbitrary C^0-bounded data, all tests, near-maximizers, or P16 supports follows.
notes.detailedSummary: For the h assumed to have v_-(h)=0, fix alpha and the explicit epsilon of n1, and take F_epsilon={smooth real F: integral exp(F)dV=1, ||F-log(h^n/(V_h dV))||_{C^{2,alpha}}<=epsilon}. All data are smooth; boundedness is in the specified C^{2,alpha} norm, with no bounds on higher derivatives. Write omega=h+dd^c u and chi as constructed in n1, Z=integral chi h wedge omega^{n-1}=integral chi omega^n, and T_F=(chi/Z)omega^{n-1}. For every test S, the pointwise matrix AM-GM inequality gives Gamma_F(S)<=exp(-b/n)omega wedge S and hence D_F(S)<=exp(-b/n). Equality holds for T_F. Any exact maximizer satisfies equality almost everywhere, so is rho omega^{n-1}; elliptic regularity and the normalized-factor uniqueness prove it equals T_F. Thus nu=(chi/Z)omega^n, q=dnu/dV=(chi/Z)(omega^n/dV), and k_T=(chi/Z)(omega^n/dV)^((n-1)/n). If a=max chi_0 and Hmax=max h^n/dV, then ||q||_infinity<=3^(n+1)a Hmax/4 and ||k_T||_infinity<=3^n a Hmax^((n-1)/n)/2. In particular p=n/(n-1) gives ||q||_p<=Cnu^(1/n) and ||k_T||_p<=Ck. Nonvacuity at the given zero-mass h is explicit: use a global smooth bump potential whose Hessian at a point is non-scalar, set omega_t=h+t dd^c psi and F_t=log(omega_t^n/((integral omega_t^n)dV)). For small t these are normalized data in the family, pairwise distinct even modulo constants, and have distinct exact maximizing currents. The sufficient condition is local strong-topology smallness; it does not imply positive global lower mass or a uniform estimate for general bounded continuous data.
notes.text:
A RESTRICTED UNIFORM CRITICAL ESTIMATE FOR EXACT MAXIMIZERS AT ZERO LOWER MASS

Theorem. Let X,h,dV be exactly as in the question, including v_-(h)=0 and n>=3. Fix 0<alpha<1. Put V=integral_X h^n, H=h^n/dV, and F*=log(H/V). Use the explicit epsilon>0 constructed in n1. Specify the density family
  F_epsilon={F in C^infinity(X,R): integral_X exp(F)dV=1,
                         ||F-F*||_{C^{2,alpha}}<=epsilon}.
The topology and quantitative bound are those of the fixed C^{2,alpha} norm in n1. All members are smooth; there is no uniform bound on derivatives of order greater than two. In particular this is also an L-infinity-bounded family of logarithmic densities, with uniformly positive upper and lower bounds on exp(F). Its normalized nature rules out nonzero constant shifts within the family.

For every F in this family every exact maximizing current has the same determinant density k_T and probability density q_T=dnu_(T,F)/dV, and
  ||q_T||_{L^infinity(dV)} <= C_nu,
  ||k_T||_{L^infinity(dV)} <= C_k,
where, writing a=max_X chi_0 and H_max=max_X H for the baseline factor of n1,
  C_nu=(3^{n+1}/4) a H_max,
  C_k=(3^n/2) a H_max^{(n-1)/n}.
Consequently, for the requested critical exponent p=n/(n-1),
  ||q_T||_{L^p(dV)} <= C_nu^{1/n},
  ||k_T||_{L^p(dV)} <= C_k.
These are uniform exact-maximizer estimates over a genuinely nontrivial infinite-dimensional specified family at the given zero-lower-mass h. The same bounds also hold if the probability-normalization condition on F is dropped and the entire small smooth C^{2,alpha} ball is used.

Proof.

1. Construction and normalization.

Apply n1 to F. It gives smooth u and b=log V+c with
  omega=h+dd^c u,   omega^n=exp(F+b)dV,
  (1/2)h<=omega<=(3/2)h,
and a smooth positive chi satisfying
  dd^c(chi omega^{n-1})=0,   integral chi h^n=1,
  chi<=3a/2.
Define
  Z=integral_X chi h wedge omega^{n-1},
  T_F=(chi/Z)omega^{n-1}.
It is a strictly positive smooth member of G_h. Since omega-h=dd^c u, integration by parts gives
  integral chi(omega-h) wedge omega^{n-1}
    =integral u dd^c(chi omega^{n-1})=0,
so
  Z=integral chi omega^n.
Pointwise positivity and comparison of omega with h give
  2^{-(n-1)}<=Z<=(3/2)^{n-1}.
These comparisons follow, for example, by diagonalizing omega relative to h: h wedge omega^{n-1}/h^n is the average of the products of n-1 eigenvalues.

2. Exact maximality, not merely near maximality.

Let S be any current in G_h. Since u is smooth and dd^c S=0,
  integral omega wedge S=integral h wedge S=1.
In the h-unitary frame let W be the positive Hermitian matrix of omega and let P=P_S be the matrix density supplied in the question. Then
  exp(F)dV/h^n=exp(-b)det W.
For positive semidefinite P and positive definite W, matrix AM-GM gives
  det(W)^{1/n}det(P)^{1/n}
    =det(W^{1/2}PW^{1/2})^{1/n}
    <=tr(WP)/n.
It follows as an inequality of measures that
  Gamma_F(S)<=exp(-b/n)omega wedge S,
and hence D_F(S)<=exp(-b/n). This argument applies equally to singular test currents.

For T_F equality holds everywhere. Indeed, for a current of the form t omega^{n-1} with smooth t>0, the trace-normalized matrix in the question is
  P=n W^{-1}/tr(W^{-1}).
Thus W^{1/2}PW^{1/2} is a scalar matrix. Consequently
  Gamma_F(T_F)=exp(-b/n)omega wedge T_F,
  D_F(T_F)=exp(-b/n).
Therefore T_F is an actual exact maximizer and M(F)=exp(-b/n). The supplied identity M(F)=exp(-B_0(F)/n) also identifies b=B_0(F). No global PDE existence theorem is needed for this identification: exact maximality was just proved directly.

For completeness, all exact maximizers equal T_F, independently of the smooth uniqueness fact supplied in the question. If S has D_F(S)=M(F), the nonnegative AM-GM deficit measure has integral zero and is zero. Therefore, sigma_S-almost everywhere,
  W^{1/2}P_S W^{1/2}=lambda I.
Since tr P_S=n, lambda=n/tr(W^{-1})>0. This is exactly the pointwise ray of omega^{n-1}, so globally S=rho omega^{n-1} for a nonnegative scalar distribution rho (a positive measure coefficient). The equation dd^c S=0 is the distributional elliptic equation A_omega rho=0, where A_omega is the operator of n1. Smooth-coefficient elliptic regularity makes rho smooth. Divide rho by integral rho h^n, which is positive and finite. The resulting factor has integral one against h^n and solves A_omega=0; the second contraction in n1 proves that it is chi. The normalization integral h wedge S=1 now forces S=(chi/Z)omega^{n-1}=T_F. This uniqueness comes from equality and ellipticity, not from the endpoint estimate.

3. Which densities are estimated.

The exact equality of measures in step 2 gives
  nu_(T_F,F)=Gamma_F(T_F)/M(F)=omega wedge T_F
            =(chi/Z)omega^n.
Thus the estimated adjoint probability density is
  q_F=dnu_(T_F,F)/dV=(chi/Z)(omega^n/dV),
and its integral is one because Z=integral chi omega^n.

Writing
  gamma=(chi/Z)^{1/(n-1)}omega,
we have T_F=gamma^{n-1}, with the required h-trace normalization. The determinant density appearing in the question is therefore
  k_{T_F}=(gamma^n/dV)^{(n-1)/n}
         =(chi/Z)(omega^n/dV)^{(n-1)/n}.
Equivalently, using omega^n/dV=exp(F+b) and M(F)=exp(-b/n),
  k_{T_F}=exp(-F/n)M(F)q_F,
which agrees exactly with the definition valid at actual maximizers. There is no conflation of k_T with the probability density q_F.

4. Uniform bounds and critical exponent.

The bounds from step 1 imply
  chi/Z <=(3a/2)2^{n-1},
  omega^n/dV <=(3/2)^n H_max.
Multiplication yields
  q_F <= (3a/2)2^{n-1}(3/2)^n H_max
        =(3^{n+1}/4)a H_max=C_nu,
and
  k_{T_F} <=(3a/2)2^{n-1}(3/2)^{n-1}H_max^{(n-1)/n}
            =(3^n/2)a H_max^{(n-1)/n}=C_k.
Since dV is a probability volume, ||k_{T_F}||_p<=C_k. Since q_F is a probability density, integral q_F^p dV<=C_nu^{p-1}; with p=n/(n-1), this gives ||q_F||_p<=C_nu^{1/n}. The bounds are actually stronger than the requested critical estimate.

5. Nonvacuity on the same h with v_-(h)=0.

The radius epsilon is strictly positive for every smooth positive h by n1. It is not a hypothesis that might secretly imply positive lower Monge-Ampere mass. No part of its construction used v_-(h)>0. Thus the family exists on every h supplied by the zero-mass premise itself.

Here is an explicit varying family inside it. Fix a point p and h-unitary holomorphic coordinates at p. Choose a smooth global real bump potential psi, adjusted to have dV-mean zero, whose complex Hessian at p is a nonzero non-scalar matrix Q. A cutoff equal to one near p times |z_1|^2-|z_2|^2 supplies such a psi. For small real t set
  omega_t=h+t dd^c psi,   V_t=integral omega_t^n,
  F_t=log(omega_t^n/(V_t dV)).
For sufficiently small t these are smooth positive forms and smooth probability log-densities, and F_t tends to F* in C^{2,alpha}. Hence an interval of these data lies in F_epsilon. Also u=t psi and b=log V_t solve the equation; taking the interval smaller makes them lie in the local contraction neighborhood of n1.

The data are pairwise distinct, not merely constant shifts. If F_s=F_t, then log(omega_s^n/omega_t^n)=log(V_s/V_t) is constant. At a maximum and a minimum of (s-t)psi, positivity and the sign of dd^c((s-t)psi) show that this constant is respectively <=0 and >=0, so it is zero. The mean-value formula for log determinants then gives
  integral_0^1 tr_{omega_t+tau(omega_s-omega_t)}
                  dd^c((s-t)psi) d tau=0.
This is a uniformly elliptic scalar equation with no zeroth-order term on the compact connected manifold. The maximum principle forces (s-t)psi constant, so s=t. Nonzero constant shifts between probability-normalized F_s,F_t are also impossible.

The exact maximizing currents in this path are themselves distinct. If T_s=T_t, their positive smooth factors show that omega_s^{n-1} and omega_t^{n-1} are on the same ray at p. The cofactor matrix identity implies that positive (1,1)-forms whose (n-1)st powers are proportional are themselves proportional. But at p the matrices are I+sQ and I+tQ; because Q is non-scalar, proportionality forces s=t. Thus this is not even a family of different data with one fixed exact current.

The entire specified normalized family is infinite-dimensional, not just this path: any sufficiently small smooth perturbation f can be normalized explicitly by
  F=F*+f-log integral exp(F*+f)dV.
The derivative of this normalization at zero is f minus its mean against exp(F*)dV, and its only constant-direction kernel is the constants. Arbitrarily many independent smooth nonconstant directions remain inside the epsilon neighborhood.

6. Scope and remaining boundary.

The proved sufficient density condition is smallness in a specified strong C^{2,alpha} topology around the explicit reference probability density h^n/V. All data in the stated family are smooth, although their higher derivatives need not be uniformly bounded. The result applies under the assumed zero lower mass because it is local in solved data and imposes no global lower mass bound on all bounded h-plurisubharmonic potentials. It does not assert an endpoint bound for arbitrary L-infinity- or C^0-bounded continuous logarithmic densities, a large C^{2,alpha} family, all normalized Gauduchon tests, or near-maximizing sequences. The full broader exact-maximizer problem in those weaker families is left unresolved. Nor is any general P16 singleton-support conclusion inferred from the endpoint estimate: the particular smooth exact-current uniqueness used here was proved separately by AM-GM equality and elliptic regularity.

This proves the sufficient-condition alternative in the task with a quantitative, genuinely nontrivial family on the given zero-lower-mass background.

reconstruction.statement:
Let X be a connected compact complex manifold of complex dimension n≥3, h a smooth positive Hermitian form, and dV a smooth positive probability volume. Assume v_-(h)=0 and use dd^c=(i/(2π))∂∂̄. Fix 0<α<1. Use the fixed norms, constants and local construction of the supporting assertion w7-1/n1; in particular put
V=∫_X h^n,  H=h^n/dV,  F_*=log(H/V),
r=min{1/(2D),1/(4KQ),m/(4GC_ADC_0)},  ε=r/(2K),
and let χ_0 be its smooth strictly positive factor with dd^c(χ_0h^{n-1})=0 and ∫_X χ_0h^n=1.

Define the family
𝓕_ε={F∈C^∞(X,ℝ):∫_X e^F dV=1 and ‖F−F_*‖_{C^{2,α}}≤ε},
with the topology induced by the fixed C^{2,α} norm. All its data are smooth. It is a bounded C^{2,α} family, with no uniform bound on derivatives of order greater than two, and
 e^{-ε}H/V≤e^F≤e^{ε}H/V.
No two members can differ by a nonzero constant.

Let 𝓖_h be the positive (n−1,n−1)-currents S with dd^cS=0 and ∫_X h∧S=1. Write σ_S=h∧S and let P_S be their positive Hermitian matrix density in an h-unitary frame, normalized by tr P_S=n and
β∧S=(1/n)tr(BP_S)σ_S,
where B is the matrix of a smooth (1,1)-form β relative to h. Define
Γ_F(S)=(e^F dV/h^n)^{1/n}det(P_S)^{1/n}σ_S,
D_F(S)=Γ_F(S)(X),  M(F)=max_{S∈𝓖_h}D_F(S).
For an exact maximizer define ν_{S,F}=Γ_F(S)/M(F).

For every F∈𝓕_ε, let u,c,ω,χ be the local solution and normalized factor furnished by w7-1/n1, so that
ω=h+dd^cu,  b=log V+c,  ω^n=e^{F+b}dV,
(1/2)h≤ω≤(3/2)h,
dd^c(χω^{n-1})=0,  ∫_X χh^n=1.
Set
Z=∫_X χh∧ω^{n-1},  T_F=(χ/Z)ω^{n-1}.
Then
Z=∫_X χω^n,  2^{-(n−1)}≤Z≤(3/2)^{n−1},
and T_F is a smooth strictly positive member of 𝓖_h. For every S∈𝓖_h, including singular currents,
Γ_F(S)≤e^{-b/n}ω∧S
as measures, and D_F(S)≤e^{-b/n}. Equality holds for T_F:
Γ_F(T_F)=e^{-b/n}ω∧T_F,  D_F(T_F)=e^{-b/n}.
Consequently
M(F)=e^{-b/n},  b=B_0(F),
and T_F is the unique exact maximizing current: every S∈𝓖_h with D_F(S)=M(F) equals T_F. If W is the matrix of ω relative to h, its trace-normalized matrix density is
P_{T_F}=nW^{-1}/tr(W^{-1}).

The adjoint/supporting probability furnished by this exact maximizer is
ν_{T_F,F}=ω∧T_F=(χ/Z)ω^n.
Its smooth positive density relative to dV is
q_F=dν_{T_F,F}/dV=(χ/Z)(ω^n/dV),  ∫_X q_F dV=1.
Define γ=(χ/Z)^{1/(n−1)}ω, so that T_F=γ^{n−1}, dd^cγ^{n−1}=0 and ∫_X h∧γ^{n−1}=1. Its determinant density is
k_{T_F}=(γ^n/dV)^{(n−1)/n}
        =(χ/Z)(ω^n/dV)^{(n−1)/n}
        =e^{-F/n}M(F)q_F,
and Γ_F(T_F)=e^{F/n}k_{T_F}dV.

Writing a=max_Xχ_0 and H_max=max_XH, put
C_ν=(3^{n+1}/4)aH_max,
C_k=(3^n/2)aH_max^{(n−1)/n}.
For every F∈𝓕_ε and every exact maximizing current T,
‖dν_{T,F}/dV‖_{L^∞(dV)}≤C_ν,
‖k_T‖_{L^∞(dV)}≤C_k.
In particular, at p=n/(n−1),
‖dν_{T,F}/dV‖_{L^p(dV)}≤C_ν^{1/n},
‖k_T‖_{L^p(dV)}≤C_k.
The same construction, exact-maximizer uniqueness, formulas and bounds hold on the entire family
𝓕̂_ε={F∈C^∞(X,ℝ):‖F−F_*‖_{C^{2,α}}≤ε},
without probability normalization of e^F dV.

The normalized family 𝓕_ε is nontrivial and infinite-dimensional on every background h satisfying the stated zero-lower-mass premise. Specifically, for every sufficiently small smooth real f in the C^{2,α} topology,
𝓝(f)=F_*+f−log∫_X e^{F_*+f}dV
belongs to 𝓕_ε. Its derivative at zero is
D𝓝_0(f)=f−∫_X f e^{F_*}dV,
whose kernel is exactly the constants; arbitrarily many independent nonconstant smooth directions remain in 𝓕_ε.

There also exist p_0∈X and a nonconstant ψ∈C^∞(X,ℝ), with ∫_X ψdV=0, such that the matrix Q of dd^cψ at p_0 in h-unitary holomorphic coordinates is nonzero and nonscalar, and there exists t_0>0 such that for every |t|<t_0,
ω_t=h+t dd^cψ>0,
V_t=∫_X ω_t^n,
F_t=log(ω_t^n/(V_t dV))∈𝓕_ε.
Here F_t→F_* in C^{2,α} as t→0, and
u_t=tψ,  b_t=log V_t
satisfy ω_t=h+dd^c u_t and ω_t^n=e^{F_t+b_t}dV, with
‖u_t‖_{C^{4,α}}+|log(V_t/V)|≤r.
For any distinct s,t∈(−t_0,t_0), F_s≠F_t, they do not differ by a constant, and their unique exact maximizing currents satisfy T_{F_s}≠T_{F_t}. The asserted critical estimates concern exact maximizers in the specified local smooth families, not all normalized Gauduchon test currents or near-maximizing sequences.
reconstruction.proof:
We use w7-1/n1 in its stated form. In particular its constants depend only on the fixed background and norms, not on a positive lower Monge–Ampère mass. We first work on the larger family F̂_ε, and impose density normalization only when discussing F_ε and its nontriviality.

1. The current produced by the local solution.

Fix F∈F̂_ε and take the smooth u,c,ω,χ supplied by w7-1/n1. Put b=log V+c and
Z=∫χh∧ω^{n-1},   T_F=(χ/Z)ω^{n-1}.
These are positive. Since dd^c(χω^{n-1})=0 and u is smooth, Stokes gives
∫χω^n-∫χh∧ω^{n-1}=∫dd^cu∧χω^{n-1}=0.
Thus Z=∫χω^n. The inequalities (1/2)h≤ω≤(3/2)h imply
2^{-(n-1)}h^n≤h∧ω^{n-1}≤(3/2)^{n-1}h^n.
Integration against χ and the normalization ∫χh^n=1 give
2^{-(n-1)}≤Z≤(3/2)^{n-1}.
The current T_F is smooth, strictly positive, dd^c-closed, and has ∫h∧T_F=1. It therefore belongs to G_h.

2. The determinant inequality, including singular tests.

Let S be any current in G_h and let σ=σ_S=h∧S. It is a probability measure. In an h-unitary frame let W be the positive matrix of ω and P=P_S the positive semidefinite measurable density with tr P=n. The Monge–Ampère equation gives
(e^F/H)^{1/n}=e^{-b/n}det(W)^{1/n}.
Consequently
Γ_F(S)=e^{-b/n}det(W^{1/2}PW^{1/2})^{1/n}σ.
For any positive semidefinite Hermitian matrix A, the arithmetic-geometric mean inequality for its eigenvalues gives det(A)^{1/n}≤tr(A)/n. This applies σ-almost everywhere and yields the measure inequality
Γ_F(S)≤e^{-b/n}(tr(WP)/n)σ=e^{-b/n}ω∧S.
No regularity of S is needed. Distributional dd^c-closedness and smoothness of u imply
∫ω∧S=∫h∧S+∫dd^cu∧S=1.
Hence D_F(S)≤e^{-b/n} for every test current, including singular ones.

For a smooth form β with h-matrix B, the elementary wedge identity is
β∧ω^{n-1}=(tr(W^{-1}B)/n)ω^n.
Applied to T_F and to β=h, it shows that
P_{T_F}=nW^{-1}/tr(W^{-1}).
Then W^{1/2}P_{T_F}W^{1/2} is scalar, so the matrix inequality is an equality. We obtain
Γ_F(T_F)=e^{-b/n}ω∧T_F,
D_F(T_F)=e^{-b/n}.
Thus the maximum is attained and M(F)=e^{-b/n}. By the scalar relation M(F)=e^{-B_0(F)/n} supplied in the task, b=B_0(F).

We prove uniqueness for all exact maximizing currents; it is not inferred from the endpoint estimate. Suppose S∈G_h satisfies D_F(S)=M(F). The nonnegative measure gap in the determinant inequality has total mass zero, so equality holds σ-almost everywhere. Since W is positive and tr P=n, tr(WP)>0. Equality in the arithmetic-geometric mean inequality therefore requires
P=nW^{-1}/tr(W^{-1})
σ-almost everywhere.

Let τ=ω∧S. Define the scalar order-zero distribution a by aω^n=τ; division by the smooth positive volume ω^n is well-defined. The preceding matrix identity and the wedge identity show, for every smooth β, that
β∧S=(tr(W^{-1}B)/n)τ=a β∧ω^{n-1}.
Thus S=aω^{n-1} as a current. Its dd^c equation becomes A_ωa=0 distributionally. The operator A_ω has smooth coefficients and positive-definite principal symbol, as established in w7-1/n1. The distributional elliptic regularity premise listed for this note therefore applies and gives a∈C^∞. It is nonnegative and nonzero because τ is a probability measure. Hence A=∫ah^n>0. The function a/A is a normalized C^{2,α} solution of A_ω(a/A)=0. The normalized-factor uniqueness in w7-1/n1 implies a/A=χ. Finally ∫h∧S=1 gives A=1/Z. Thus S=T_F. This proves uniqueness even among singular candidate maximizers.

3. The adjoint probability and determinant density.

The exact equality above gives
ν_{T_F,F}=Γ_F(T_F)/M(F)=ω∧T_F=(χ/Z)ω^n.
It follows that its smooth positive dV density is
q_F=(χ/Z)(ω^n/dV),   ∫q_F dV=1.
This also directly verifies the adjoint property. For L_ωv=n(dd^cv∧ω^{n-1})/ω^n and every smooth v,
∫L_ωv q_F dV=(n/Z)∫dd^cv∧χω^{n-1}=0.
The supporting property may either be imported from the task or checked directly: for another logarithmic density G,
M(G)≥D_G(T_F)=M(F)∫exp((G-F)/n)dν_{T_F,F}.
Jensen's inequality and the given M=e^{-B_0/n} relation yield
B_0(G)≤B_0(F)-∫(G-F)dν_{T_F,F}.
This is the supporting inequality with the appropriate negative sign.

Define γ=(χ/Z)^{1/(n-1)}ω. It is a smooth positive Hermitian form and
γ^{n-1}=T_F,   dd^cγ^{n-1}=0,   ∫h∧γ^{n-1}=1.
Its determinant density is therefore
k_{T_F}=(γ^n/dV)^{(n-1)/n}
=(χ/Z)(ω^n/dV)^{(n-1)/n}.
Using ω^n/dV=e^{F+b} and M(F)=e^{-b/n} gives
k_{T_F}=e^{-F/n}M(F)q_F,
Γ_F(T_F)=e^{F/n}k_{T_F}dV.
These formulas respect the h-trace normalization because γ^{n-1}=T_F is precisely the normalized current used above.

4. Uniform critical estimates.

Write a_0=max_Xχ_0 and H_max=max_XH. The supporting construction gives
χ≤(3/2)a_0,   Z^{-1}≤2^{n-1},   ω^n/dV≤(3/2)^nH_max.
Consequently
q_F≤(3/2)a_0·2^{n-1}·(3/2)^nH_max
=(3^{n+1}/4)a_0H_max=C_ν,
and
k_{T_F}≤(3/2)a_0·2^{n-1}·((3/2)^nH_max)^{(n-1)/n}
=(3^n/2)a_0H_max^{(n-1)/n}=C_k.
Every exact maximizing current equals T_F, so these bounds hold for every exact maximizer in the specified family.

For p=n/(n-1), positivity and ∫q_FdV=1 imply
∫q_F^p dV≤C_ν^{p-1},
whence ||q_F||_{L^p(dV)}≤C_ν^{(p-1)/p}=C_ν^{1/n}.
Because dV is a probability volume, ||k_{T_F}||_{L^p(dV)}≤||k_{T_F}||_{L^∞(dV)}≤C_k. This proves both asserted endpoint estimates, in fact through stronger uniform L^∞ estimates.

Nothing in steps 1–4 required ∫e^FdV=1. The constructions, uniqueness, formulas, and constants therefore apply to the whole smooth C^{2,α} ball F̂_ε as claimed.

5. Quantitative description and nontriviality of the normalized family.

Now impose ∫e^FdV=1. The family F_ε consists entirely of smooth data and is bounded in the fixed C^{2,α} norm, with that norm's induced topology. The pointwise bound |F-F_*|≤ε gives
 e^{-ε}H/V≤e^F≤e^{ε}H/V.
If F and G in this family satisfy F-G=d for a constant d, normalization gives 1=e^d, hence d=0. Thus constant shifts do not account for its nontriviality.

Let μ_*=e^{F_*}dV=h^n/V, a smooth positive probability measure, and define
N(f)=F_*+f-log∫e^f dμ_*.
For every smooth f this is smooth and normalized. Since
|log∫e^f dμ_*|≤||f||_{C^0},
it lies in F_ε for all sufficiently small f in C^{2,α}; the threshold depends only on ε and the fixed norm of the constant function. Differentiating at zero gives
DN_0(f)=f-∫f dμ_*.
Its kernel is exactly the constants. More strongly, N(f)=N(g) implies that f-g is constant. Hence arbitrarily high-dimensional subspaces of smooth functions modulo constants yield injectively parametrized small families in F_ε. The family is nontrivial and infinite-dimensional.

No higher-derivative restriction is being hidden here. It is possible even to see that no uniform integer-order derivative bound above order two holds on this family. Choose a coordinate patch, a smooth cutoff equal to one on a smaller patch, and a real coordinate x_1. For integers j tending to infinity set
f_j=δ j^{-(2+α)}cutoff·cos(jx_1),
extended by zero. The usual Hölder product estimates and |cos(jx)-cos(jy)|≤min(2,j|x-y|) give ||f_j||_{C^{2,α}}≤Cδ uniformly. Choosing δ>0 small enough puts N(f_j) in F_ε. On the region where the cutoff is one, derivatives of any integer order k≥3 have sizes comparable to δj^{k-2-α}, which are unbounded. Normalization subtracts only a constant, and the fixed smooth F_* cannot cancel this divergence. Thus higher derivative bounds are neither required nor implicit in the specified family.

These conclusions hold for every fixed background satisfying v_-(h)=0: F_* itself exists and the entire normalization construction above remains available. This proves nonvacuity of the density condition under the stated antecedent, without asserting the existence of a zero-lower-mass background independently of that antecedent.

6. A path with distinct data and distinct exact maximizers.

Fix p_0 and holomorphic coordinates centered there that make h(p_0) unitary. Choose a cutoff equal to one near p_0, multiply it by |z_1|^2, extend by zero, and subtract its dV mean. Call the resulting function ψ. It is smooth, nonconstant, and ∫ψdV=0. The h-matrix Q of dd^cψ at p_0 is nonzero and nonscalar: it has a nonzero first diagonal entry and zero remaining entries. The stipulated dd^c normalization only changes that nonzero entry by a positive fixed factor.

For small |t|, compactness gives ω_t=h+t dd^cψ>0. Let V_t=∫ω_t^n>0 and
F_t=log(ω_t^n/(V_t dV)).
These functions are smooth, satisfy ∫e^{F_t}dV=1, and tend to F_* in C^{2,α}. Shrink t_0>0 so that for every |t|<t_0,
||F_t-F_*||_{C^{2,α}}≤ε,
||tψ||_{C^{4,α}}+|log(V_t/V)|≤r.
The pair u_t=tψ and b_t=log V_t has the required mean-zero normalization and solves ω_t^n=e^{F_t+b_t}dV.

To identify it with the local solution and to prove distinctness, we record smooth-solution uniqueness using the listed maximum principle. Suppose two smooth positive solution forms h+dd^cu_1 and h+dd^cu_2 solve the equation with the same F and scalars b_1,b_2. At a maximum of u_1-u_2 their matrices are ordered ω_1≤ω_2, so b_1≤b_2. At a minimum the opposite ordering gives b_1≥b_2. Thus b_1=b_2. The logarithmic determinant identity used above now gives a smooth scalar uniformly elliptic equation with no zeroth-order term for u_1-u_2, using the inverses of the positive convex combinations of the two forms. On the connected compact manifold the difference attains a maximum, so the maximum-principle premise of this note makes it constant. Equal dV-mean normalizations make that constant zero. All coefficients here are smooth and the convex combinations remain uniformly positive on the compact manifold, so the stated premise applies. This proves that u_t,b_t agree with the local construction. It also shows that F_s=F_t forces (s-t)ψ=0, and hence s=t. Nonzero constant differences are excluded by probability normalization.

Finally suppose T_{F_s}=T_{F_t}. Each is a strictly positive scalar multiple of the (n-1)st power of its corresponding ω. Equality of such powers at p_0 forces ω_s(p_0) and ω_t(p_0) to be conformal. Indeed the matrix of the complementary-degree power of a positive matrix A is proportional to det(A)A^{-1}; proportional such matrices imply proportional A's. Thus, for some λ>0,
I+sQ=λ(I+tQ).
Because Q is nonscalar, I and Q are linearly independent. Comparing their coefficients gives λ=1 and s=t. Therefore distinct parameters give distinct exact maximizing currents as well as distinct normalized data.

The result is a genuine restricted-family uniform theorem at zero lower mass: it assumes quantitative smallness in the smooth C^{2,α} topology and estimates either the adjoint density q_F or the trace-normalized determinant density k_T. It does not estimate all Gauduchon test currents or near-maximizers, nor does it settle larger merely continuous bounded density families. No singleton-support conclusion of P16 is inferred from the endpoint estimate; the exact-maximizer uniqueness used here was proved separately by equality and elliptic regularity.

All four exact premise strings are established. For premise 0, I reconstructed the stated Hölder-space version from Oh’s compact-manifold Sobolev Fredholm theorem, Dyatlov’s smooth-kernel result, and Simon’s interior Schauder estimates. Closed-range duality and distributional elliptic regularity identify the cokernel with smooth solutions of the formal adjoint relative to dμ. Differentiation, interpolation, and a finite coordinate cover give the stated higher-order Schauder estimates, including the C^{s,α}-coefficient interior variant. [Oh, Proposition 10.1.13](https://cgp.ibs.re.kr/~yongoh/all.pdf), [Simon, Lecture 12](https://math.stanford.edu/~lms/lecs-on-pde.pdf).

Premise 1 follows from Cass’s Theorem 7.1, localized in manifold charts. Premise 2 follows from local constancy of the Banach-space Fredholm index; the Laplace–Beltrami index is zero because its kernel and adjoint kernel coincide, with the Hölder realization preserving these smooth kernels. [Cass](https://www.math.ubc.ca/~cass/research/pdf/FS.pdf), [Analysis on Manifolds, Theorem 1.5.2](https://www.staff.science.uu.nl/~ban00101/geoman2017/AS-2017.pdf).

Premise 3 matches the c≤0 strong maximum principle, with the minimum formulation obtained by replacing v with −v. Its applications to L_h and the shifted adjoint have the required ellipticity and signs. [MIT, Lecture 6, Theorem 4](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-156-differential-analysis-spring-2004/d9e0f047d5682a70799331a926d27a11_lec6.pdf). No positive lower Monge–Ampère mass hypothesis is required by these external results.

passages.statement: Let M be a compact smooth manifold without boundary, dμ a smooth positive density, 0<α<1, and s a nonnegative integer. Let P be a real scalar second-order differential operator with smooth coefficients and uniformly positive-definite symmetric principal coefficient matrix. Then P:C^{s+2,α}(M)→C^{s,α}(M) is Fredholm, its kernel consists of smooth functions, and its range is exactly the set of f satisfying ∫_M f p dμ=0 for every smooth p with P* p=0, where P* is the formal adjoint relative to dμ. Moreover, ||v||_{C^{s+2,α}}≤C(||Pv||_{C^{s,α}}+||v||_{C^0}) for a constant determined by P, M and the fixed norms. The analogous interior Schauder estimates hold on coordinate domains for uniformly elliptic operators whose coefficients belong to C^{s,α}.

primary_source_audit.root_interior_schauder_cross_assessment: Simon gives the complete constant-coefficient lemma for k=2m and the freezing/absorption argument in divergence form. For nondivergence order two, freeze a^{ij} at the ball center, apply that same k=2 constant-coefficient lemma to a compactly supported cutoff of u, and estimate the error (a(center)-a(x))D2u by its small oscillation times the highest Holder seminorm plus the bounded coefficient Holder seminorm times the D2u supremum. Interpolation absorbs the latter and cutoff first derivatives. A finite cover yields the C0-term estimate. Differentiating the equation gives higher-order estimates for C^(s,alpha) coefficients; no smooth-density argument in full Holder norm is required. The paper uses the separately read Taylor smooth-coefficient parametrix mapping for its two inverse maps and Taylor nonlinear regularity for its smooth bootstrap.

source_check_limits: The article derives full Holder compatibility from compact Sobolev Fredholm theory and the actual order-minus-two parametrix Holder mapping, rather than assuming smooth density in full Holder norms. Exact author-hosted Taylor passages and printed proofs were read, including the nonlinear elliptic bootstrap. The article includes an explicit strong maximum/minimum principle barrier proof. Every immutable native source binding is retained separately; no claim is made to have read every recursively referenced source.
publication_limits: This is a completely proved explicit sufficient-density condition in a small strong-topology family on the given zero-lower-mass background. It is not a theorem for all Gauduchon tests, near-maximizers, arbitrary continuous bounded log-densities or large Holder balls. Exact-current uniqueness is proved separately and does not imply general P16 singleton supports. Model checks support mathematical assessment and are not journal review. No full original catalogue closure or book rebuild is claimed.
